headword: {三角定規|さんかくじょうぎ}

definitions.explanation: A triangular drafting tool used for drawing straight lines and angles. In Japan, students typically use a set of two: one with 30-60-90 degree angles and one with 45-45-90 degree angles.

examples.japanese: {三角定規|さんかくじょうぎ}で{線|せん}を{引|ひ}いた。
examples.english: I drew a line with a set square.

examples.japanese: {算数|さんすう}の{授業|じゅぎょう}で{三角定規|さんかくじょうぎ}の{使|つか}い{方|かた}を{習|なら}った。
examples.english: We learned how to use a set square in math class.

examples.japanese: {二|ふた}{種類|しゅるい}の{三角定規|さんかくじょうぎ}を{組|く}み{合|あ}わせると、いろいろな{角度|かくど}の{線|せん}が{引|ひ}ける。
examples.english: By combining two types of set squares, you can draw lines at various angles.

notes:
USAGE:
A standard school supply in Japan. Elementary school students learn to use set squares in arithmetic class. The two standard types are the 30-60-90 triangle and the 45-45-90 triangle. Part of the standard stationery set alongside a ruler ({定規|じょうぎ}), compass (コンパス), and protractor ({分度器|ぶんどき}).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {三角定規|さんかくじょうぎ}で{角度|かくど}を{測|はか}る (to measure angles with a set square)
- {三角定規|さんかくじょうぎ}のセット (a set of triangle rulers)
